newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Firmer crown seen postponing Swedish repo hike.
newsitem.headline: Firmer crown seen postponing Swedish repo hike.

text.p: A strengthening of the Swedish crown could postpone an expected hike in the key repurchase rate until next summer, economists said on Monday.
"It's possible that the crown will reach its 1996 level of 114-115 on the TCW (trade weighted index) at the end of the year," Bengt Hansson, senior economist at Handelsbanken, told Reuters.
"In that case the crown would slow down inflation and the Riksbank could wait with tightening (monetary policy) until next summer."

Hansson previously expected the central bank to raise the repo rate in January or February next year after keeping it at 4.10 percent this year. The repo is the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
The Riksbank cut the repo sharply last year, bringing it down to its current level on December 17 from 8.91 percent at the start of 1996.

The crown has firmed to 119.56 on the TCW index from a year-high of 124.24 on May 5 and from 117.63 at the end of last year. The Riksbank, which does not have a target for the crown, has set the appropriate level at 109-118 in real terms.
The crown has also strengthened against the mark, changing hands at 4.2845 on Monday and firming from 4.5850 on March 18, its softest level this year, and from 4.4420 at the end of 1996.

But along with most other currencies, the crown has lost ground against the dollar, trading at 7.9668 on Monday, slightly firmer than 8.0810 on August 5, its softest level since 1994, but much weaker than the 6.8459 at which it closed 1996.

The crown's rebound against the mark was triggered by market turmoil with a sharply stronger dollar, a softer mark and worries about Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) which made players focus on Swedish fundamentals, analysts said.

"The private sector has been growing since 1995, industrial production development is strong and so is foreign trade, with trade and current account surpluses," said Hansson, who sees the crown at 4.20 to mark in a month.

The stronger crown was seen postponing a repo hike as it would put a lid on inflation, which amounted to 0.8 percent in June, well below the Riksbank's target of one percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side.

But some economists saw the crown's firming largely as a recovery from its spring softness -- caused by companies paying out large dividends abroad and bond coupons expiring -- and have not changed their repo forecasts.
"We see the crown firming another percent," said Knut Hallberg, senior economist at Swedbank, still forecasting a rate hike in the first six months of next year.
But Sven-Arne Svensson, chief economist at Hagstromer & Qviberg, said the Riksbank could very well cut the repo.
"Our official forecast is that the repo will remain flat until next summer but I don't want to exclude a cut if inflation continues to surprise (by staying lower than expected)," he said.

Svensson saw the crown firming one percent on the TCW index in six months and two percent in a year while he expected its advance against the mark to level off, seeing it trading between 4.20 and 4.30 to the German currency this autumn.
Economists did not expect the stronger crown to have much of an adverse effect on export companies as it was just recovering from a weak level.
"I don't think there is a large danger," Svensson said.

"Industrial production has risen seven to eight percent so far this year and the crown will on average be softer this year than last year when it was trading at 116 on the TCW index on average, so Swedish competitiveness has actually strengthened."
Economists largely dismissed the notion that the Riksbank, according to dealers, intervened twice last week and said the bank probably followed its policy to smooth out sudden fluctuations.
